name: Alabama
description: Alabama requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has a lemon law that covers new vehicles purchased or leased in Alabama, and does not require emissions testing statewide.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Alabama's new-vehicle lemon law is Ala. Code §§ 8-20A-1(8), 8-20A-2. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The lemon law rights period is one year after original delivery or the first 12,000 miles, whichever comes first. That is the window for first giving notice of the nonconformity. The repair presumption itself is measured during the 24 months after delivery or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first, and at least one repair attempt must fall inside the rights period. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair three or more times, plus a final attempt by the manufacturer, and it continues, or the vehicle is out of service for repair, including the final attempt, for a cumulative total of 30 calendar days. Before a lawsuit the consumer must send notice of the nonconformity by certified mail. If the presumption has already arisen, the manufacturer gets a final cure: seven calendar days to name a repair facility, then 14 calendar days after delivery to conform the vehicle.
registrationNotes: Alabama charges a flat registration fee plus additional county-level taxes. Title fees are $18. Plates must be renewed annually by the owner's birthday.

name: Alaska
description: Alaska has some of the most unique vehicle ownership requirements in the nation. While liability insurance is mandatory, the state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Alaska's new-vehicle lemon law is AS 45.45.320. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption runs during the term of the express warranty or the one-year period after delivery to the original owner, whichever period terminates first. There is no mileage cap. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair three or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service for repair for a total of 30 or more business days. Time when repairs are not performed for reasons beyond the repairer's control is excluded. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. Chapter 20, SLA 2024 (HB 233), effective October 27, 2024, rewrote who counts as the repairer; the three-repair and 30-business-day thresholds were not changed. The only adopted floor amendment added 'and fractions of an hour' to a warranty-labor time-allowance clause. Written notice demanding a refund or replacement must be mailed before 60 days have elapsed after the express warranty or the one-year period ends, whichever terminates first. Within 30 days after receiving that notice, the manufacturer may make a final repair attempt. That 30-day final-attempt window is not the presumption; the presumption is 30 or more business days out of service.
registrationNotes: Alaska charges a biennial registration fee of $100 for most passenger vehicles. There is no state sales tax, but some municipalities charge local taxes on vehicle purchases.

name: Arizona
description: Arizona vehicle owners benefit from relatively low insurance minimums but must comply with emissions testing in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas. The state offers incentives for electric and alternative fuel vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arizona's new-vehicle lemon law is Ariz. Rev. Stat. §§ 44-1262, 44-1264. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. Repairs and the presumption run during the shorter of the express-warranty term or the period of two years or 24,000 miles after original delivery, whichever is earlier. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of thirty or more calendar days. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. The presumption does not apply against a manufacturer unless the manufacturer has received prior direct written notification of the alleged defect and has had an opportunity to cure it. That notice requirement is not a separate day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas for vehicles older than five model years. Vehicles are tested every other year. Testing costs approximately $17.
registrationFeeRange: $8 base fee plus vehicle license tax
registrationNotes: Arizona charges a low base registration fee of $8 but adds a vehicle license tax based on assessed value. New vehicles are assessed at 60% of MSRP, decreasing by 16.25% each year.

name: Arkansas
description: Arkansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers. The state does not mandate emissions testing but does require annual safety inspections in some counties.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arkansas's new-vehicle lemon law is Ark. Code §§ 4-90-403(12), 4-90-406, 4-90-410. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The motor vehicle quality assurance period ends 24 months after original delivery or at the first 24,000 miles of operation attributable to the consumer, whichever is later. The statute uses "whichever is later," not whichever comes first. After three attempts on the same nonconformity that substantially impairs the vehicle, or after one attempt on a nonconformity likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, the consumer gives certified or registered mail notice so the manufacturer has a final cure. A separate rebuttable presumption arises if that repair path was followed and the nonconformity continues, or the vehicle is out of service for repair a cumulative total of 30 calendar days, or there have been five or more attempts on separate occasions to repair nonconformities that together substantially impair use and value. The manufacturer has ten days after the written notice to offer a reasonably accessible repair facility, then ten days after delivery to conform the vehicle. If it misses those periods, the final-attempt requirement drops and a nonrebuttable presumption arises.
registrationNotes: Arkansas registration fees are based on vehicle weight. An annual personal property tax is also assessed on vehicles. Title transfers cost $10.

name: California
description: California has the most comprehensive vehicle regulations in the country, including strict emissions standards, generous EV incentives, and strong consumer protection laws including a robust lemon law.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: California's new-vehicle lemon law is Cal. Civ. Code § 1793.22. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The Tanner presumption applies within 18 months from delivery to the buyer or 18,000 miles on the odometer, whichever occurs first. That window is the presumption period, not the full term of the express warranty. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if, in that window, the same nonconformity likely to cause death or serious bodily injury has been subject to repair two or more times, or the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of more than 30 calendar days. Direct manufacturer notice is required for the two-repair and four-repair prongs only if the manufacturer clearly and conspicuously disclosed that requirement. Buyer notice to the manufacturer is a condition of asserting the two-repair and four-repair prongs, and only if the manufacturer disclosed the notice requirement in the warranty or owner's manual. It is not a separate earlier day-count presumption. The out-of-service presumption is more than 30 calendar days, not a 15-day notice trigger.
emissionsDetails: California requires biennial smog checks for vehicles older than eight model years in most areas. The state sets its own emissions standards through CARB, which are stricter than federal standards. Testing typically costs $30-$70.
evIncentiveDetails: California's statewide CVRP rebate closed November 8, 2023. Income-qualified residents who scrap an older vehicle can apply for Clean Cars 4 All (cleancars4all.arb.ca.gov) before buying, and many California utilities offer EV charger rebates and EV rates.
registrationNotes: California charges a base registration fee of $46, a vehicle license fee (0.65% of vehicle value), plus various surcharges. Total first-year costs for a new vehicle can exceed $400. Renewal is annual.

name: Colorado
description: Colorado combines mandatory liability insurance with emissions testing in the Denver metro area. The state is a leader in EV incentives, offering substantial tax credits for electric vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Colorado's new-vehicle lemon law is Colo. Rev. Stat. § 42-10-103. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. As amended by SB 24-192 (signed June 6, 2024, effective August 7, 2024, and applicable to motor vehicles sold or leased on or after that date), the presumption window is the first 24,000 miles or two years after original delivery, whichever occurs earlier. The prior statute used the warranty term or one year, four repair attempts, and 30 business days. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair three or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of twenty-four or more business days, or a safety-based nonconformity has been subject to two or more repair attempts and continues to exist. Each alternative is measured within the first 24,000 miles or two years, whichever occurs earlier. The presumption does not apply unless the manufacturer has received prior written notification by certified mail and has been provided ten business days to cure after receipt. Those ten business days are a post-notice cure opportunity, not the out-of-service presumption. The cure attempt counts as one repair.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the Denver-Boulder-Greeley-Fort Collins metro area for vehicles 4-11 model years old. Testing is performed at Air Care Colorado stations and costs approximately $25.
evIncentiveDetails: Colorado offers a state EV tax credit of $750 in 2026 for new EVs with an MSRP up to $80,000, plus an additional $2,500 for EVs with an MSRP under $35,000 (Colorado Energy Office). Dealers can apply the credit at purchase. Leases must be at least two years.
registrationNotes: Colorado registration fees are based on vehicle weight and taxable value. A specific ownership tax is assessed that decreases with vehicle age. Registration is annual, due on the owner's birth month.

name: Connecticut
description: Connecticut requires emissions testing for most vehicles and has strong consumer protection laws. The state mandates relatively high insurance minimums compared to the national average.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Connecticut's new-vehicle lemon law is Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-179. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The four-repair and 30-day presumption runs during the two years after original delivery or the first 24,000 miles, whichever period ends first. The separate safety presumption uses a different window: the express warranty term or one year after original delivery, whichever ends first. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of thirty or more calendar days, during the two-year or 24,000-mile period. If a nonconformity is likely to cause death or serious bodily injury if the vehicle is driven, the presumption instead arises after repair at least twice within the express warranty or one year after delivery, whichever ends first. The consumer need not notify the manufacturer unless the manufacturer has clearly and conspicuously disclosed, in the warranty or owner's manual, that written notification is required before a refund or replacement. That disclosure rule is not an earlier day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Biennial emissions testing is required for most vehicles registered in Connecticut. Testing follows the OBD-II protocol for vehicles 4+ model years old. Cost is approximately $20.
evIncentiveDetails: Connecticut's CHEAPR program offers $1,500 for new battery EVs (from October 15, 2026) and $500 for plug-in hybrids at participating dealers. Income-qualified Rebate+ buyers can receive up to $4,500 on a new battery EV.
registrationNotes: Connecticut charges a biennial registration fee of $80 for most passenger vehicles. A supplemental fee applies to vehicles with a value above $50,000. Title fee is $25.

name: Delaware
description: Delaware requires liability insurance and biennial vehicle inspections. The state has no sales tax on vehicle purchases, which can represent significant savings for car buyers.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Delaware's new-vehicle lemon law is Del. Code tit. 6, § 5004. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption applies within the warranty term or during the period of 1 year following original delivery, whichever is the earlier date. There is no mileage cap. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if substantially the same nonconformity has been subject to repair or correction 4 or more times and continues to exist, or the automobile is out of service by reason of repair or correction for a cumulative total of more than 30 calendar days. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. The presumption does not apply against a manufacturer unless the manufacturer has received prior direct written notification and has had an opportunity to repair or correct the nonconformity. That notice condition is not a separate day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Delaware requires biennial emissions testing for vehicles in New Castle County that are more than 4 model years old. Testing uses OBD-II diagnostics and costs approximately $20.
safetyInspectionDetails: Delaware requires biennial safety inspections for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, windshield, exhaust, and other safety systems. Cost is approximately $35-$50 at authorized inspection stations.
registrationNotes: Delaware charges a flat registration fee and a 4.25% document fee on the purchase price in lieu of sales tax. Title fee is $55. No state sales tax applies to vehicle purchases.

name: Florida
description: Florida is a no-fault insurance state, meaning your own insurance covers your injuries regardless of who caused the accident. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $10,000 personal injury protection (PIP) / $10,000 property damage liability. Bodily injury liability is only required if the driver has had license or registration suspended.
lemonLawSummary: Florida's new-vehicle lemon law is Fla. Stat. §§ 681.102(9), 681.104. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The Lemon Law rights period, defined in Fla. Stat. § 681.102(9), is the period ending 24 months after the original delivery of the motor vehicle. There is no mileage cap. It is not the manufacturer's warranty term. During the Lemon Law rights period, a reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair at least three times, plus a final manufacturer attempt if undertaken under § 681.104(1)(a), and the nonconformity continues to exist, or the vehicle has been out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of 30 or more days (60 or more days for a recreational vehicle). The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. Day 15 is not the presumption. Fla. Stat. § 681.104(1)(b) requires written notice by registered or express mail when the vehicle is out of service for a cumulative total of 15 or more days, so the manufacturer can inspect or repair. After three attempts on the same nonconformity, § 681.104(1)(a) requires separate written notice giving the manufacturer a final repair attempt. The presumption in § 681.104(3) is three repairs or 30 or more cumulative days.
registrationNotes: Florida registration fees are based on vehicle weight. An initial registration fee applies, plus a $225 new wheels fee for first-time registrations. Title fee is $77.25 including lien recording.

name: Georgia
description: Georgia requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the metro Atlanta area. The state replaced its traditional sales tax on vehicles with a one-time title ad valorem tax (TAVT).
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Georgia's new-vehicle lemon law is O.C.G.A. §§ 10-1-782, 10-1-784. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The lemon law rights period ends two years after original delivery of a new motor vehicle to a consumer or at the first 24,000 miles of operation, whichever occurs first. It is not the express-warranty term. O.C.G.A. § 10-1-782 defines 'days' as calendar days. During the lemon law rights period, a reasonable number of attempts is deemed undertaken if a serious safety defect has been subject to repair one time and has not been corrected, or the same nonconformity has been subject to repair three times and has not been corrected, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair of one or more nonconformities for a cumulative total of 30 days. After a reasonable number of attempts, the consumer notifies the manufacturer, which then has 28 days from receipt to make a final repair attempt. That 28-day final attempt follows the presumption; it is not an earlier day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the 13-county metro Atlanta area for vehicles 3-25 model years old. Annual OBD-II testing costs $25 at Georgia Clean Air Force stations.
registrationNotes: Georgia charges a $20 annual registration fee plus a title ad valorem tax (TAVT) of 7% of the vehicle's fair market value at the time of purchase. This replaces the traditional annual ad valorem tax.

name: Hawaii
description: Hawaii requires all registered vehicles to pass a periodic safety inspection. The state has mandatory no-fault insurance and offers growing incentives for electric vehicles as part of its clean energy goals.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $10,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: Hawaii's new-vehicle lemon law is Haw. Rev. Stat. §§ 481I-2, 481I-3. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The lemon law rights period is the term of the manufacturer's express warranty, the period ending two years after original delivery, or the first 24,000 miles of operation, whichever occurs first. During the lemon law rights period, a reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to examination or repair at least three times and continues to exist, or a nonconformity likely to cause death or serious bodily injury has been subject to examination or repair at least once and continues, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of thirty or more business days. The presumption does not apply unless the manufacturer has received a written report of the nonconformity and has had a reasonable opportunity to repair it. Separately, upon a second notice of the nonconformity, or if the vehicle has been out of service by reason of repair in excess of twenty business days, the dealer shall notify the manufacturer. That 20-business-day dealer notice is not the presumption; the presumption is thirty or more business days.
emissionsDetails: Oahu requires annual emissions inspections for gasoline-powered vehicles as part of the safety inspection process. Other islands only require safety inspections.
safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles in Hawaii. Inspections cover brakes, lights, tires, steering, and exhaust systems. Cost is typically $20-$30.
registrationNotes: Hawaii charges a state registration fee plus a county-specific vehicle weight tax that varies by island. Registration is annual. Title fee is $5.

name: Idaho
description: Idaho has relatively low insurance requirements and does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most personal vehicles. The state has a straightforward registration process.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Idaho's new-vehicle lemon law is Idaho Code § 48-903. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption window is the applicable express warranty term, or two years after original delivery, or the date the mileage reaches 24,000 miles, whichever is the earliest date. If the nonconformity was first reported during the express warranty, attempts that occur within three years after delivery can still support a refund or replacement. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of thirty or more business days. If the nonconformity is a complete failure of the braking or steering system and is likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, the presumption arises after repair at least once, but the manufacturer must still have at least one repair opportunity before the presumption arises. The four-repair and 30-business-day presumption applies against the manufacturer only if the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer has received prior written notification at least once and an opportunity to cure. That written-notice condition is not a separate day-count presumption.
registrationNotes: Idaho registration fees are based on the age of the vehicle, ranging from $69 for newer vehicles to $45 for those over 8 years old. An additional county fee and plate fee may apply.

name: Illinois
description: Illinois requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Chicago metro area and Metro East St. Louis. The state has a strong lemon law and offers incentives for electric vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Illinois's new-vehicle lemon law is 815 ILCS 380/2, 815 ILCS 380/3. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption arises within the statutory warranty period. 815 ILCS 380/2 defines that period as one year or 12,000 miles, whichever occurs first after delivery of the new vehicle. It is a period created by the Act, not the term of the manufacturer's express warranty. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if, within the statutory warranty period, the same nonconformity has been subject to repair 4 or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle has been out of service by reason of repair of nonconformities for a total of 30 or more business days. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. The presumption does not apply unless the manufacturer has received prior direct written notification from or on behalf of the consumer and has an opportunity to correct the alleged defect. That notice condition is not a separate day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the greater Chicago area and Metro East St. Louis region for most vehicles 4-13 model years old. OBD-II testing is used, and testing costs $20.
evIncentiveDetails: The Illinois EPA EV rebate cycle runs August 1 to December 31, 2026: $2,000, or $4,000 for low-income applicants. Applications must be made within 180 days of purchase.
registrationNotes: Illinois charges an annual registration fee of $151 for standard passenger vehicles. Electric vehicles pay an additional $100 annual fee. Title fee is $150.

name: Indiana
description: Indiana requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law covering new car purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Indiana's new-vehicle lemon law is Ind. Code §§ 24-5-13-7, 24-5-13-8, 24-5-13-15. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The term of protection ends the earlier of eighteen months after original delivery or 18,000 miles after that date. The buyer must report the nonconformity within that term. Section 24-5-13-15 does not restate a separate months-or-miles limit on the repair count itself. The statute calls this a term of protection, not the manufacturer's warranty term. A reasonable number of attempts is considered undertaken if the nonconformity has been subject to repair at least four times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair of any nonconformity for a cumulative total of at least thirty business days and the nonconformity continues to exist. The chapter states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. A buyer must first notify the manufacturer of a claim if the manufacturer made the disclosure required by Ind. Code § 24-5-13-9. That notice duty is not an earlier day-count presumption.
registrationNotes: Indiana charges a base registration fee of $21.35 plus an annual excise tax based on the vehicle's value and age. The excise tax decreases as the vehicle ages.

name: Iowa
description: Iowa requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but does have some of the most affordable vehicle registration fees in the nation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Iowa's new-vehicle lemon law is Iowa Code §§ 322G.2, 322G.4. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The lemon law rights period is the term of the manufacturer's written warranty, the period ending two years after original delivery, or the first 24,000 miles of operation attributable to a consumer, whichever expires first. Iowa Code § 322G.2 defines 'days' as calendar days. During the lemon law rights period, a reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same substantially impairing nonconformity has been subject to examination or repair at least three times, plus a final manufacturer attempt if undertaken, and continues to exist; or a nonconformity likely to cause death or serious bodily injury has been subject to examination or repair at least one time, plus that final attempt if undertaken, and continues to exist; or the vehicle has been out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of thirty or more days. Twenty days is not the presumption. After twenty or more cumulative days out of service, the consumer may give written notice, and the manufacturer then has ten cumulative out-of-service days to conform the vehicle. Written notice for a final cure may also be given after three attempts on the same nonconformity, or after one attempt on a nonconformity likely to cause death or serious bodily injury. The presumption in § 322G.4(3) is three repairs, one safety repair, or thirty or more calendar days.
registrationFeeRange: 1% of value annually, decreasing with age
registrationNotes: Iowa charges a fee-for-new-registration that is 5% of the purchase price, plus an annual registration fee based on the vehicle's book value (1% for the first year, decreasing to a minimum). Title fee is $25.

name: Kansas
description: Kansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. Some counties in the Kansas City metro area require emissions testing. The state has a relatively straightforward registration process.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Kansas's new-vehicle lemon law is Kan. Stat. Ann. § 50-645. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The four-repair and 30-day prongs run within the term of any warranty or during the one year after original delivery, whichever is the earlier date. There is no mileage cap. If the manufacturer receives actual notice, a reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of 30 or more calendar days, or there have been 10 or more attempts to repair any nonconformities that substantially impair use and value. The statute states no lower repair count limited to a serious safety defect. The 10-attempt sentence does not itself restate the one-year or warranty window. The presumption is introduced by the condition that the manufacturer receives actual notice of the nonconformity. That notice condition is not a separate day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Johnson and Wyandotte counties (Kansas City metro area) for vehicles 4+ model years old. Biennial OBD-II testing costs approximately $17.
safetyInspectionDetails: Kansas requires a safety inspection when a vehicle is first registered in the state. Annual inspections are not required for most vehicles after initial registration.
registrationNotes: Kansas registration fees are based on vehicle weight. Personal property taxes are also assessed on vehicles. Registration is annual.

name: Kentucky
description: Kentucky requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on all vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Kentucky's new-vehicle lemon law is Ky. Rev. Stat. § 367.842. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption runs within the first 12,000 miles of operation or during the twelve months following original delivery, whichever is the earlier date. The statute does not define that window as the manufacturer's warranty term. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity, defect, or condition has been subject to repair four or more times and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair of the same nonconformity for a cumulative total of at least thirty calendar days. The out-of-service count is for the same defect, not an accumulation of unrelated defects. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. If the manufacturer cannot repair the nonconformity after a reasonable number of attempts during that window, the buyer shall report the nonconformity in writing to the manufacturer. That written report follows the repair attempts; it is not an earlier day-count presumption.
registrationNotes: Kentucky charges a $21 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles plus county clerk fees. A 6% usage tax applies to vehicle purchases. Personal property tax is assessed annually.

name: Louisiana
description: Louisiana requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state requires periodic safety inspections but does not mandate emissions testing statewide.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Louisiana's new-vehicle lemon law is La. Rev. Stat. § 51:1943. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The presumption runs within the warranty term or during a period of one year following original delivery, whichever is the earlier date. There is no mileage cap. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of forty-five or more calendar days, or the same nonconformity has been subject to repair four or more times. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. The replacement-or-refund duty in La. Rev. Stat. § 51:1944 uses the same four-attempt and 45-calendar-day figures. If the manufacturer fails to respond to the consumer or to perform the repairs within the time periods described in § 51:1943(A), the manufacturer waives a final attempt to cure. That waiver is not a separate earlier day-count presumption.
safetyInspectionDetails: Louisiana requires an annual or biennial safety inspection for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, lights, horn, mirrors, and tires. Cost is typically $10-$20.
registrationNotes: Louisiana registration fees are based on the vehicle purchase price. Vehicles priced under $10,000 pay $20, while more expensive vehicles pay up to $82. License plate fees vary by parish.

name: Maine
description: Maine requires liability insurance and annual vehicle inspections. The state has a strong lemon law and participates in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, promoting cleaner transportation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Maine's new-vehicle lemon law is Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 10, § 1163. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The repair duty and the presumption run during the term of the express warranties, within 3 years after original delivery, or during the first 18,000 miles, whichever occurs earliest. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to a repair attempt 3 or more times and continues to exist, or the same nonconformity has resulted in a serious failure of either the braking or steering systems and has been subject to a repair attempt one or more times, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of a repair attempt for a cumulative total of 15 or more business days. The consumer gives written notice of a desire for a refund or replacement so the manufacturer has a final repair opportunity for the 7 business days following receipt. That notice can be given after one repair attempt if the nonconformity resulted in a serious failure of the braking or steering systems. The 7 business days are a final-repair window, not the presumption. The presumption is 15 or more business days out of service.
emissionsDetails: Maine follows California's CARB emissions standards and requires OBD-II emissions testing in Cumberland County for vehicles older than the current plus one model year. Testing is annual.
safetyInspectionDetails: Maine requires annual safety inspections for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, steering, exhaust, glass, and other safety components. Cost is typically $12.50.
evIncentiveDetails: Efficiency Maine offers income-qualified EV rebates when paired with an off-peak charger: $7,000 new / $3,000 used for low-income buyers and $5,000 new / $2,000 used for moderate-income buyers.
registrationNotes: Maine charges an annual registration fee based on vehicle weight, typically $35 for most passenger vehicles. Excise tax is also assessed based on the vehicle's MSRP and age.

name: Maryland
description: Maryland requires liability insurance, safety inspections for vehicle transfers, and has a strong lemon law. The state mandates emissions testing and offers growing EV incentive programs.

lemonLawSummary: Maryland's new-vehicle lemon law is Md. Code Ann., Com. Law §§ 14-1501, 14-1502. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The manufacturer's warranty period, defined in § 14-1501, is the earlier of the motor vehicle's first 18,000 miles of operation or 24 months after original delivery. That definition does not extend any manufacturer's express warranty. It is not a 15-month or 15,000-mile period. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair 4 or more times within the warranty period and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair for a cumulative total of 30 or more days during the warranty period, or a nonconformity resulting in failure of the braking or steering system has been subject to the same repair at least once within the warranty period, the manufacturer has been notified and given an opportunity to cure, and the repair does not bring the vehicle into compliance with the state's motor vehicle safety inspection laws. During the warranty period the consumer reports the nonconformity by certified mail, return receipt requested, and the corrections shall be completed within 30 days of the manufacturer's receipt of that notification. That 30-day completion duty after notice is separate from the presumption's cumulative 30 or more days out of service.
emissionsDetails: Maryland requires biennial emissions testing in most counties for vehicles 4+ model years old using OBD-II testing. The Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) test is free at state-operated stations.
safetyInspectionDetails: Maryland requires a safety inspection when a vehicle is sold or changes ownership. The inspection covers major safety systems. Cost varies by inspection station, typically $60-$100.
evIncentiveDetails: Maryland's EV excise tax credit currently has no funding; applicants are placed on a waiting list.
registrationNotes: Maryland charges a biennial registration fee based on vehicle weight. The state also charges a 6% excise tax on vehicle purchases. Title fee is $100.

lemonLawSummary: Massachusetts's new-vehicle lemon law is Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 7N 1/2. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The term of protection is one year or fifteen thousand miles of use from original delivery, whichever comes first. The statute defines a business day as any day during which the service departments of authorized dealers of the manufacturer are normally open for business. The term of protection is not the manufacturer's warranty term. A reasonable number of attempts is deemed undertaken if the same nonconformity has been subject to repair three or more times within the term of protection and continues to exist or recurs within the term of protection, or the vehicle is out of service by reason of repair of any nonconformity for a cumulative total of fifteen or more business days during the term of protection. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. The manufacturer is afforded one additional opportunity, not to exceed seven business days, to cure. No consumer shall be required to give notice directly to a manufacturer of a nonconformity before resorting to state-certified new-car arbitration. The additional manufacturer cure, not to exceed seven business days, begins when the three-repair or 15-business-day limit has been met or exceeded. It is not an earlier day-count presumption.
emissionsDetails: Massachusetts requires annual emissions testing as part of the combined safety and emissions inspection for vehicles older than the current plus one model year. OBD-II testing is used.

registrationNotes: Massachusetts charges a $60 biennial registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A 6.25% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $75.

lemonLawSummary: Michigan's new-vehicle lemon law is Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 257.1402, 257.1403. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The consumer must initially report the defect during the manufacturer's express warranty or not later than 1 year from delivery to the original consumer, whichever is earlier. The four-repair presumption is then measured within 2 years of the date of the first repair attempt. The days-out presumption is measured during the express warranty or within 1 year from delivery, whichever is earlier. There is no mileage cap. A reasonable number of attempts is presumed if the same defect or condition that substantially impairs use or value has been subject to repair a total of 4 or more times within 2 years of the first repair attempt and continues to exist, or the vehicle is out of service because of repairs for a total of 30 or more days or parts of days during the express warranty or within 1 year from delivery, whichever is earlier. The statute states no lower repair count for a serious safety defect. Before using the remedy, and any time after the third repair attempt on the same defect, the consumer must give written notification by return receipt service so the manufacturer can cure; after delivery to the designated facility the manufacturer has 5 business days to repair. On the days-out path, written notice is required after the vehicle has been out of service for at least 25 days in a repair facility, and the manufacturer then has 5 business days to repair. The third-repair notice and the 25-day notice are triggers for a final cure, not the presumption. The presumption is 4 repairs or 30 or more days.

lemonLawSummary: Minnesota's new-vehicle lemon law is Minn. Stat. § 325F.665. The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. If the nonconformity results in a complete failure of the braking or steering system and is likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, the presumption arises after repair at least once and the nonconformity continues to exist. The four-repair and 30-business-day presumption applies against the manufacturer only if the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer has received prior written notification at least once and an opportunity to cure. The statute attaches that written-notice condition to paragraph (b), the four-repair and 30-day presumption, rather than to the separate brake-or-steering presumption. lemonLawSummary: South Dakota's new-vehicle lemon law is SDCL 32-6D-5; lemon law rights period defined in SDCL 32-6D-1. No lower safety-defect count. Before a civil action, § 32-6D-6 requires notice of a nonconforming condition by certified mail to the manufacturer and a demand for correction or repair. lemonLawSummary: Virginia's new-vehicle lemon law is Va. Code § 59.1-207.13(B); lemon law rights period defined in § 59.1-207.11. lemonLawSummary: Washington's new-vehicle lemon law is RCW 19.118.041(2); eligibility period defined in RCW 19.118.021(6). The figures in this paragraph were checked against that statute on October 22, 2026. The eligibility period ends two years after original delivery or at the first twenty-four thousand miles, whichever occurs first. For the presumption, the manufacturer's written warranty shall be at least one year after original delivery or the first twelve thousand miles, whichever occurs first. Motor homes have separate attempt and day counts in RCW 19.118.041(3). For a new motor vehicle other than a motor home, within the eligibility period: the same serious safety defect diagnosed or repaired two or more times and it continues; the same nonconformity diagnosed or repaired four or more times and it continues; the vehicle out of service for diagnosis or repair a cumulative total of thirty calendar days, at least fifteen of them during the written warranty; or, within a twelve-month period, two or more different serious safety defects each diagnosed or repaired at least once. A motor home uses one serious-safety attempt plus a final attempt, three repairs of the same nonconformity plus a final attempt, or sixty cumulative calendar days out of service. For a motor home, after one serious-safety attempt, after three attempts on the same nonconformity, or after thirty or more cumulative days out of service, the consumer must give written notice so the motor home manufacturers can make a final coordinated attempt. For other new motor vehicles, RCW 19.118.041(1) requires a written request to a manufacturer office before replacement or repurchase, which follows a reasonable number of attempts.
